key_insight: Higher-order parity constraints can improve QAOA success probabilities beyond resolving hardware connectivity limits, apparently by accelerating correlation propagation.
engineering_relevance: Parity-based QAOA offers a promising route to better optimization on sparse quantum hardware using parameters trained on smaller instances.
method: Apply selected parity transformations to Signed Max-Cut on 3-regular graphs.
Classically optimize QAOA parameters on training instances with up to 14 vertices.
Transfer parameters to larger instances on IBM Heron processors and apply error mitigation.
evidence_signal: In tests up to 40 vertices, parity-based QAOA with error mitigation found optimal solutions for every tested 40-vertex instance, while conventional QAOA failed under the same conditions.
watch_item: Results are limited to the tested instances; broader generalization and the hardware overhead of higher-order operators require further evaluation.
paper_title: Higher-order Parity Constraints for Quantum Approximate Optimization
